questions.title: Drain a Min-Heap PriorityQueue
questions.description:
Practice the two core PriorityQueue habits: adding elements and draining them. Read n distinct integers, insert every one into a PriorityQueue, then repeatedly poll the queue and print each removed element. With natural ordering the polled values come out in ascending order.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
One line per polled element, in the order they are removed (ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000

questions.title: Peek Versus Poll Demonstration
questions.description:
Demonstrate that peek() only reads the head of a PriorityQueue while poll() removes it. Read n distinct integers into a PriorityQueue, print the head once using peek(), then poll every element and print it. The head value therefore appears twice: once from peek and once as the first polled element.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
First line: Head: X where X is the value returned by peek().
Then n lines: Polled: Y for each element in poll order (ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000

Polled: 27

questions.title: Task Scheduler Runs Jobs By Priority
questions.description:
A continuous integration server runs pending jobs one at a time; every job has a name and a priority number, and a smaller priority number means the job runs earlier. All priorities are distinct. Read every job, put the priorities into a PriorityQueue, then simulate execution by repeatedly polling the smallest priority and printing the name of the job that carries it.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name priority where name is a single word and all priorities are distinct.

Output Format:
One line per executed job: the job name, in execution order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500; priorities are distinct integers with 1 <= priority <= 1000000

questions.title: PriorityQueue With Descending Comparator
questions.description:
By default a PriorityQueue is a min-heap. To serve the largest element first you must supply a Comparator that reverses the natural order. Read n distinct integers into a PriorityQueue built with such a hand-written comparator, then poll everything and print each removed value. The printed sequence must be strictly descending.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
One line per polled element, in descending order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000

questions.title: PriorityQueue Query Simulator
questions.description:
Simulate a PriorityQueue through commands. ADD x inserts x; PEEK prints the smallest element without removing it; POLL prints and removes the smallest element; SIZE prints the number of stored elements. When the queue is empty, PEEK and POLL print Empty.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q (number of commands).
Next q lines: one command each, either ADD x, PEEK, POLL or SIZE.

Output Format:
One line for every PEEK, POLL and SIZE command; ADD produces no output.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; ADD values are integers with absolute value <= 1000000

questions.title: Hospital Triage Queue
questions.description:
A hospital emergency room gives every arriving patient a token; a smaller token number means the patient is seen earlier, and all tokens are distinct. Process the shift log: ARRIVE name token queues a patient, NEXT prints the name of the next patient without serving them, SERVE serves and prints the name of the next patient, COUNT prints how many patients are still waiting. With nobody waiting, NEXT and SERVE print No patients.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q.
Next q lines: one query each: ARRIVE name token, NEXT, SERVE or COUNT.

Output Format:
One line for every NEXT, SERVE and COUNT query; ARRIVE produces no output.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; tokens are distinct positive integers <= 1000000; names are single words

questions.title: K Largest Readings With a Size-K Min-Heap
questions.description:
A weather sensor gateway receives n distinct readings but has room to remember only the k most extreme ones. Keep a min-heap (a PriorityQueue with natural ordering) of at most k elements: for every new reading, if the heap already holds k values and the reading is larger than the smallest, replace the smallest. Afterwards the heap contains exactly the k largest readings; print them from largest to smallest.

Input Format:
First line: the integers n and k.
Second line: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
k lines: the k largest values in descending order, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 100000; all n integers are distinct; each value has absolute value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Minimum Cost To Connect Ropes
questions.description:
A construction crew must join n ropes into one long rope. Joining two ropes costs the sum of their lengths, and the cheapest strategy always joins the two currently shortest ropes. Use a min-heap: repeatedly poll the two smallest lengths, add their sum to the total cost, and insert the combined rope back until only one rope remains.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated rope lengths.

Output Format:
One line: the minimum total joining cost (0 when n is 1).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= length <= 1000000; the answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer

questions.title: HashMap Command Console
questions.description:
Drive a HashMap from commands to see exactly what put, get, containsKey and size return. PUT k v stores the pair and prints the value that was previously stored under k (print null when the key is new); GET k prints the stored value or null; CONTAINS k prints true or false; SIZE prints the number of stored pairs.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q.
Next q lines: one command each: PUT k v, GET k, CONTAINS k or SIZE.

Output Format:
One line for every PUT, GET, CONTAINS and SIZE command.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; keys and values are single-word tokens

questions.title: Stock Update Overwrite Trail
questions.description:
A tiny inventory tracker records stock deliveries as pairs of sku and quantity. The first time a sku appears it is inserted; later entries overwrite the old quantity. Print an audit line for every entry and finish with the number of distinct skus stored in the map.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: sku qty.

Output Format:
For a new sku: sku: inserted qty.
For an overwrite: sku: old -> new.
Last line: Size: N where N is the number of distinct skus.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= qty <= 1000000; skus are single-word tokens

questions.title: Contact Book Manager
questions.description:
Manage a phone contact book backed by a HashMap. ADD name number stores a contact and prints Added; FIND name prints the stored number or Not found; DELETE name prints Deleted when the contact existed (and removes it) or Not found; COUNT prints how many contacts are stored.

Input Format:
First line: the integer q.
Next q lines: one query each: ADD name number, FIND name, DELETE name or COUNT.

Output Format:
One line for every query.

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 100000; names and numbers are single-word tokens; numbers have up to 10 digits

questions.title: Warehouse Stock Auditor
questions.description:
A warehouse auditor processes stock movements and leaves an audit trail. RECEIVE sku qty registers a new sku (printing a registration line) or restocks an existing one (printing the new total); SHIP sku qty is only allowed when the sku exists and its stock is at least qty, otherwise the shipment is denied. Use containsKey guards rather than getOrDefault. After all movements print how many distinct skus the warehouse holds.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: RECEIVE sku qty or SHIP sku qty.

Output Format:
For a new sku: sku registered with qty.
For a restock: sku restocked to newtotal.
For an accepted shipment: sku shipped, remaining left.
For a denied shipment: sku shipment denied.
Last line: SKUs: N.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= qty <= 1000000; skus are single-word tokens

The college cafeteria keeps its menu in a map from item name to price. Build the menu first, then handle counter queries: PRICE item prints the price or Unavailable; UPDATE item price changes the price and prints a confirmation, or reports that the item is not on the menu; COUNT prints how many items the menu currently has.

Next n lines: item price (items are distinct).
Next line: the integer q.
Next q lines: PRICE item, UPDATE item price or COUNT.

Output Format:
One line for every query.

Constraints:
1 <= n, q <= 100000; 1 <= price <= 1000000; items are single-word tokens

questions.title: Aggregate Student Marks Alphabetically
questions.description:
Every line of a marks sheet names a student and the marks they scored on one assessment; a student may appear many times. Aggregate the totals per student, then print one line per student with their total, ordered alphabetically by name. A TreeMap keeps its keys sorted, which makes the output order automatic.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name marks.

Output Format:
One line per distinct student, alphabetically by name: name total.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= marks <= 100; names are single-word tokens

questions.title: Contest Leaderboard Top-K
questions.description:
A coding contest leaderboard receives score updates; every update names a player and sets their current total score (a later update for the same player replaces the earlier score). After reading all updates and a number k, print the top k players ordered by score descending; players with equal scores are ordered alphabetically by name. Aggregate latest scores in a TreeMap, then sort the names with a two-level comparator.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: name score.
Next line: the integer k.

Output Format:
k lines: name score, from highest score to lowest, alphabetical for ties.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= number of distinct names <= n <= 100000; 0 <= score <= 1000000000

questions.title: First Unique Login ID Report
questions.description:
A security script scans a login log of n integer user ids and reports anomalies. An id is unique if it appears exactly once in the whole log. Print the first unique id in the original log order (or -1 when every id repeats), and on a second line print how many distinct ids are unique. Count occurrences with a HashMap, then scan the original order; never rely on map iteration order for the first-unique answer.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the first id occurring exactly once, or -1 if there is none.
Line 2: the number of distinct ids that occur exactly once.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= id <= 1000000000

questions.title: Print Shop Job Dispatcher
questions.description:
A print shop queues jobs; each job has an id and a priority number where a smaller number means printed earlier, and every (priority, id) pair is distinct. Read all jobs, then a dispatch threshold T. Simulate dispatching: always take the pending job with the smallest priority, breaking ties by the smaller id. Jobs whose priority is at most T are printed as they are dispatched; jobs with a larger priority are deferred. Finish with the deferred count. Store each job as a two-element int array in a PriorityQueue ordered by a hand-written comparator.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n.
Next n lines: jobId priority.
Last line: the threshold T.

Output Format:
One line jobId priority for every dispatched job whose priority <= T, in dispatch order.
Last line: Deferred: X.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= jobId <= 1000000000; 1 <= priority <= 1000000; all (priority, jobId) pairs are distinct; 0 <= T <= 1000000

questions.title: Sort Characters By Frequency
questions.description:
A text analysis tool reports how often each letter of a word appears, most frequent first. Read a lowercase word, count every character with a HashMap, then sort the distinct characters by count descending and break ties alphabetically ascending. Print one line per distinct character with its count.

Input Format:
One line: the word (lowercase letters only, no spaces).

Output Format:
One line per distinct character: ch count, ordered by count descending, then alphabetically ascending.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100000; the word contains only the letters a to z

questions.title: Character Frequency Report
questions.description:
Build a simple frequency report: read a word and print how many times each character occurs, listing the characters in alphabetical order. A TreeMap keyed by Character iterates its entries in sorted key order, so the report comes out sorted automatically.

Input Format:
One line: the word (lowercase letters only, no spaces).

Output Format:
One line per distinct character in alphabetical order: ch count.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100000; the word contains only the letters a to z

questions.title: Polling Booth Vote Counter
questions.description:
A polling booth records n votes, each for one candidate name. Afterwards officials ask queries: VOTES name prints how many votes that name received (0 if it never appeared) and WINNER prints the candidate with the most votes followed by their total, breaking ties by the alphabetically first name. Count votes in a HashMap and determine the winner by scanning an alphabetically sorted list of candidate names.

Input Format:
First line: the integer n (number of votes).
Next n lines: one candidate name per line.
Next line: the integer q.
Next q lines: VOTES name or WINNER.

Output Format:
For VOTES: the vote count as a number.
For WINNER: name total of the leader.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= q <= 100000; names are single-word tokens
